correctness.rationale: Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:1505.04672v1 yields F/L=E q(U²)^(d-1), U~Beta(d,n-d+1), after binomial/Beta normalization. Multiplying by U² tilts to Beta(d+2,n-d+1). The sinc-square-root kernel q is strictly convex on [0,1] by its cosine integral and positive second derivative; hence the secant deficit h=(1-q^(d-1))/z is strictly decreasing. Beta stochastic ordering gives strict R_(n+1)>R_n; bounded convergence gives limit and the n=d+1 simplex gives the sharp other endpoint. Analytic quantifiers include all dimensions at least two and sample sizes at least dimension plus one, and both strictness/equality conditions. An executed 144-case 55-digit verifier supplements but does not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: A finite limiting mean facet number has a natural quadratic-order sampling bias. Prior work identifies its leading asymptotic, but the result supplies an exact all-sample-size shape law for its scale-corrected error and two best constants. At n=d+1 the lower bound is attained; at infinite sample size the upper coefficient is optimal. These are mathematically meaningful global quantitative bounds beyond numerical evaluation.
